document.title: The Ionization and Dynamics of the Makani Galactic Wind Submitted to ApJ ABSTRACT The Makani galaxy hosts the poster child of a galactic wind on scales of the circumgalactic medium. It consists of a t

tldr.text: Combining shock models, density-sensitive line ratios, and mass and velocity measurements, we estimate that the ionized mass and outflow rate in the Episode II wind could be as high as that of the molecular gas: M HII II ∼ M H2 II = (1 − 2) × 109 M⊙ and dM/dtHII II ∼ dM/dtH2 II = 170 − 250 M⊙ yr−1.
The fast, inner wind extending to RII = 20 kpc— Episode II—is powered by a young starburst of age 7 Myr (Rupke et al. 2019) and star formation rate 224– 300 M⊙ yr−1 (Petter et al. 2020).

problem.text: The momentum and energy in the recent Episode II wind imply a momentum-driven flow (p “boost” ∼7) driven by the hot ejecta and radiation pressure from the Eddington-limited, compact starburst.
The ionized mass of either wind episode is unknown, however, and since no other gas phases have yet been observed in the extended Episode I wind, we do not know its outflow rate.

approach.text: It consists of a two-episode wind in which the slow, outer wind originated 400 Myr ago (Episode I; RI = 20 − 50 kpc) and the fast, inner wind is 7 Myr old (Episode II; RII = 0 − 20 kpc).
Here we present Keck optical spectra of the Makani outflow.

Using line ratios and the luminosity of recombination lines, we conclude that the ionized gas in the inner wind is energized by fast, vs = 400 km s−1 shocks moving through a low-density nH ∼ 10 cm−3 medium (Allen et al. 2008), consistent with earlier results (Perrotta et al. 2021).
